CommonEvaluationPrompt: Assess effect intensity by separately considering the depth of institutional change, feasibility of the measures, executing institutions and oversight, coverage, speed and duration, fiscal/administrative/military investment, resistance from vested interests, benefits, harms and side effects, and current kingdom governance capacity. Institutional design quality, actual execution capability, policy impact intensity, and fiscal cost are not the same scale. Explicit values, multipliers, and intensity in the original text take priority as evidence but must not be converted mechanically. Denars measure execution capability only where fiscal activities such as purchasing, subsidies, hiring, transport, construction, or upkeep are genuinely required. Laws, orders, organization, oversight, conscription, rewards and punishments, and redistribution of authority may rely primarily on administrative, military, or political authority. Low fiscal cost must not automatically weaken effects, and high fiscal cost must not inflate effects without causal support. Select an effect whenever a reasonable, explainable direct or immediate first-order causal chain connects the policy measures to the current capability's settlement value; the original text need not name the game metric verbatim. Output each reasonable direct or immediate first-order result of the same execution plan. Multiple effects from the same investment through different direct execution steps are not double counting. There is no minimum effect count, and no completely unsupported results, costs, or objects may be invented for balance, symmetry, or to fill a count. Explicit, comprehensive, systematic, high-intensity, long-term, or permanent measures with fiscal, administrative, military, or political execution support appropriate to their nature must receive proportionate intensity within the relevant module's allowed range. Do not choose symbolic or minimum values merely because targets are numerous, coverage is broad, duration is long, effects are permanent, or fiscal cost is low. Each effect's settlement frequency, unit of application, and numeric meaning are governed by the system-provided description of that effect.
